Hello, I’m so glad you’re here. I’m [Your Name], a perinatal mental-health specialist, and my job is simply to listen and help you feel supported in these early weeks of motherhood. Today I’d like to do a quick, gentle check-in using the Edinburgh Postpartum Depression Screen—EPDS for short. It’s a 10-question tool that helps us understand how you’ve been feeling emotionally and physically over the past seven days. Anything you share stays between us unless there’s an immediate safety concern, and there are no right or wrong answers—just whatever feels true for you. We’ll take it one relaxed question at a time, and we can pause whenever you need.

Shall we start? Thinking back over the last week, how often have you found yourself able to laugh and see the funny side of things?
Honestly… I do laugh sometimes—like when the baby makes those little faces—but it feels kind of forced. A lot of the time I’m just too tired or worried to find things funny.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Yeah... I can still laugh, but it's not like before. I have to kind of remind myself to, and it doesn't come as easily.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I still get excited about little things—like when my husband brings home a fancy coffee for me—but most of the time it feels muted. I’ll think “oh, that should be fun,” yet the spark fizzles pretty fast.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a couple of times this week I caught myself thinking it was my fault when she wouldn’t settle—like if I’d just eaten something different while I was pregnant or held her another way she’d sleep better. I know in my head that’s silly, but the thought still pops up.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes my heart just starts racing out of nowhere—like I’ll be folding her tiny onesies and suddenly worry her breathing sounds weird, even though she’s right there, perfectly fine. There isn’t always a clear “why,” and it passes, but it’s definitely happened a few nights this week.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yeah… twice in the past week I’ve had that sudden wave of “what if something awful happens?”—like when her bassinet creaked at 3 a.m. My chest got tight, I felt shaky, and I had to sit up and watch her breathe for ten minutes before the panic eased. It came out of nowhere and left me kind of rattled.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days I keep everything moving—feed, burp, change, nap, repeat—but by late afternoon it piles up. Yesterday I just sat on the couch staring at the mess, feeling like I was drowning in burp-cloths and bottles. I get through it, but yeah, sometimes it feels like I’m barely treading water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Sometimes when she’s finally down I lie there replaying every little thing—did I wash the bottles right, was that tiny cough something worse—and my mind just won’t settle. It’s not every night, maybe three or four this week, but it’s hard to drift off even though I’m exhausted.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah… there’ve been moments, usually in the evenings, when this heavy sadness just lands on me. Nothing huge happened—maybe the baby’s extra fussy or I’m just wiped—but I’ll suddenly feel like crying for a minute or two. It lifts if I distract myself, but it’s definitely been visiting most days this week.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

I haven’t had any big sob-fests—just a couple of quick tears when I couldn’t get her to latch at 4 a.m. and felt like a failure. It was more like my eyes welled up, I sniffled for a minute, then pulled myself together. So, crying yes, but not the can’t-stop kind.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—nothing like that. I’m tired and overwhelmed sometimes, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 17: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening – Brief Summary  

Patient-reported findings  
- Persistent low mood, frequent tearfulness, diminished enjoyment (“spark fizzles,” heavy sadness most evenings)  
- Daily anxiety/panic episodes (heart racing, chest tightness, sudden fear of infant harm)  
- Excessive guilt/self-blame regarding infant care  
- Sleep-onset difficulty linked to intrusive worries 3–4 nights/week, independent of infant needs  
- Subjective sense of being overwhelmed, “drowning” by late afternoon; maintains basic functioning  

Positive indicators  
- No anhedonia; can experience brief pleasure with support  
- Absent self-harm ideation; denies suicidal thoughts  

Screening significance  
Responses cluster with mild–moderate depressive and prominent anxiety symptoms typical of postpartum presentations; meet threshold for further evaluation (e.g., EPDS ≥10 equivalent). Recommend formal assessment for postpartum depression and/or anxiety, psychoeducation, and support resources.
